newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backed spreads narrow as prices dive.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backed spreads narrow as prices dive.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities slid as much as 3/4 of a point in some coupons on Friday, but spreads over Treasuries narrowed.

A stronger-than-expected December employment report rattled the fixed-income markets early in the day. Treasuries dove more than a point and a half after the news, and mortgages followed them down, mortgage experts said.
Traders said they saw wide variety of market plays.
"There's been buying, there's been selling," said one trader who cited a lot of up-in-coupon trades.
Late Friday afternoon, mortgages were off 6/32 to 25/32 overall. Losses spread rather evenly across the spectrum, with premium coupons suffering least.
Spreads over Treasuries had tightened about five basis points narrower.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 15/32 at 99-19/32, yielding 97 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 14/32 at 99-18/32, while Freddie Mac paper had declined 14/32 to stand at 99-24/32.
The 10-year note was off 20/32, yielding 6.62 percent.
The December jobs report showed payrolls expanded by 262,000 last month as the unemployment rate held at 5.3 percent. Average hourly earnings rose 0.5 percent to $12.05.
